executiveSummary: Surveillance reports from ECDC (weeks 16-20, 2026) and PAHO (October 2025 through May 2026) indicate multiple concurrent disease threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) — a BSL-3 select agent — has generated multiple epidemiological updates in the Americas region, representing the most significant zoonotic spillover risk in the surveillance window. Additional elevated concerns include Mpox circulating in the Americas, Yellow Fever activity, and the onset of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season coinciding with RSV circulation. Dengue, Chikungunya, Measles, Pertussis, and Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome represent ongoing regional burdens requiring sustained monitoring.
bottomLine: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) zoonotic activity in the Americas and simultaneous multi-pathogen circulation across both hemispheres represent the highest-priority threats in this surveillance cycle.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained zoonotic activity
BSL-3 select agent with documented human spillover risk and pandemic potential
Persistent circulation in avian and mammalian reservoirs across multiple Americas countries
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interfaces; ensure rapid diagnostic capacity and antiviral stockpile readiness; coordinate with USDA/CDC on farm-level containment and healthcare worker PPE protocols

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 confirming ongoing transmission in the Americas
Concurrent global clade I expansion elevates risk of importation of more virulent strains
BSL-3 select agent requiring enhanced biosafety and case investigation protocols
threats.action: Strengthen genomic sequencing to discriminate clade I from clade II; expand vaccination to high-risk populations; reinforce cross-border surveillance and contact tracing

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 2026 during a period historically associated with high dengue burden
Hyperendemicity across tropical Americas with risk of severe dengue and healthcare system strain
Co-circulation with Chikungunya virus in shared Aedes aegypti transmission zones
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations; ensure hospital surge capacity for severe dengue; alert clinicians to differentiate from Chikungunya and Zika

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active transmission risk
BSL-3/select agent status; high case fatality rate in unvaccinated individuals
Epizootics in non-human primates serve as sentinel events for human spillover risk
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in endemic and border regions; investigate primate die-offs as early warning signals; ensure vaccine supply chains are uninterrupted

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and RSV
threats.pathogen: Influenza A/B viruses; Respiratory Syncytial Virus
threats.location: Americas Region (Southern Hemisphere onset); Europe (ECDC weeks 16-20)
signals: PAHO alert April 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
Concurrent RSV and influenza circulation flagged January 2026 creating dual-burden respiratory emergency risk
ECDC weekly threat reports weeks 16-20 tracking respiratory virus activity in Europe
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination uptake; prepare ICU and pediatric surge capacity; monitor for novel reassortant influenza strains; ensure RSV prophylaxis availability for high-risk infants

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two sequential PAHO epidemiological updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained elevated incidence
Resurgence pattern consistent with waning vaccine immunity and potential acellular vaccine escape
Elevated risk to unvaccinated infants and immunocompromised individuals
threats.action: Audit maternal Tdap vaccination coverage; investigate laboratory-confirmed cases for antibiotic resistance markers; reinforce cocooning strategy in neonatal care settings

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert February 2026 indicating active transmission in the context of post-pandemic immunity gaps
Risk of re-establishment of endemic transmission in areas with suboptimal MMR coverage
Importation risk from regions with ongoing outbreaks
threats.action: Conduct sub-national vaccination coverage assessments; implement supplementary immunization activities in low-coverage areas; strengthen laboratory confirmation capacity

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert December 2025 highlighting HPS activity
High case fatality rate (30-50%) with no approved antiviral treatment
Seasonal rodent population dynamics and human encroachment drive exposure risk
threats.action: Enhance rodent surveillance in endemic rural areas; educate high-risk populations on exposure prevention; ensure critical care capacity for respiratory failure management

selectAgentSummary: Three BSL-3 select agents are identified in this surveillance cycle. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) represents the most urgent concern with two PAHO updates (November 2025, March 2026) documenting ongoing zoonotic activity across the Americas, posing pandemic preparedness implications. Mpox virus has triggered a dedicated PAHO update (April 2026) with potential for clade I importation into the Americas raising virulence concerns. Yellow Fever virus prompted a PAHO alert in March 2026, with epizootic signals warranting vaccination campaign verification. All three require enhanced biosafety protocols, rapid genomic characterization, and international coordination under IHR frameworks.

diseases: Communicable disease threats (ECDC weeks 16-20 2026 — influenza, respiratory, and other circulating pathogens)

amrSignals: Bordetella pertussis: concern for potential acellular vaccine antigen divergence and macrolide resistance in some regional isolates — warrants systematic susceptibility testing
Influenza viruses: ongoing surveillance needed for oseltamivir resistance markers in circulating H5N1 and seasonal strains given antiviral prophylaxis use in exposed workers
General AMR concern: co-infections during influenza/RSV season may drive empiric antibiotic overuse, accelerating resistance in community respiratory pathogens
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen respiratory burden (H5N1, seasonal influenza, RSV) creating diagnostic ambiguity and healthcare system stress across both hemispheres
Sequential PAHO alerts on Pertussis (Dec 2025, Mar 2026) suggest sustained resurgence rather than isolated outbreak, consistent with waning immunity at population level
Co-circulation of Dengue and Chikungunya in Aedes-endemic zones increases risk of misdiagnosis and under-reporting of severe cases
Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset (April 2026) overlapping with active H5N1 zoonotic activity raises theoretical reassortment risk requiring enhanced genomic surveillance
GLP-1 receptor agonist misuse alert (Feb 2026) reflects emerging intersection of pharmaceutical supply chain risks and public health — a non-traditional surveillance signal
